Adam (the First Man)
AD-uhm
proper noun (Old Testament figure)
Adam (Hebrew Adam) means "man" and is connected with adamah, the ground from which he was formed; the proper name of the first man.

📖 Biblical Definition

Adam was the first man, formed by God of the dust of the ground, into whose nostrils the LORD breathed the breath of life so that he became a living soul. Created in the image of God, male and female, given dominion over the creatures and set in the garden of Eden, Adam was constituted not merely the first of the race but its federal head and representative. To him God gave the covenant of works, with the tree of the knowledge of good and evil as its test; and when Adam ate, he sinned not for himself alone but for all his posterity descending from him by ordinary generation. As the apostle teaches, by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin, and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned. Thus the guilt of Adam's first transgression is imputed to his seed, and a corrupt nature conveyed to them, the original sin of the whole race. Yet Adam is set forth in Scripture as the figure of Him that was to come, for as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive. The first Adam was made a living soul; the last Adam, the Lord Jesus Christ, a quickening spirit. So the federal headship of Adam unto condemnation is answered by the federal headship of Christ unto justification and life, the very hinge of the gospel.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The first man and federal head of the human race, by whose disobedience sin and death came upon all, set forth as the figure of Christ the last Adam.

expand to see more

ADAM, proper noun. From the Hebrew for "man," akin to adamah, ground; the first man, formed of the dust.

Created in the image of God and made the federal head of his posterity.

By his first transgression sin and death entered the world and passed upon all men.

As it is written, "For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive" (1 Cor 15:22).

A figure of Him that was to come, answered by Christ the last Adam, a quickening spirit.

📖 Key Scripture

Gen 2:7 — "And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul."

Rom 5:12 — "Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned:"

1Co 15:22 — "For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive."

1Co 15:45 — "And so it is written, The first man Adam was made a living soul; the last Adam was made a quickening spirit."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The historicity of Adam is widely denied today, his fall reduced to myth and his federal headship dismissed, undermining the gospel itself.

expand to see more

The chief assault on Adam in our day is the denial that he ever lived—the reduction of the first man to a symbol, an archetype, or a poetic figure standing for humanity in general rather than a real individual created by God at the beginning. This is no minor revision. If there was no historical Adam who really sinned, then there is no real imputation of guilt, no original sin transmitted to the race, and the apostle's argument in Romans 5 and First Corinthians 15 collapses. Paul reasons from a true and historical Adam to a true and historical Christ; deny the one and you wound the other.

The principle to recover is the federal headship of Adam and the parallel headship of Christ, which together form the architecture of the gospel. Adam was constituted the covenant representative of all his natural posterity, so that his fall is our fall and his guilt our guilt. Against this stands the last Adam, the Lord Jesus, whose obedience and sacrifice are imputed to all who are in Him by faith. As in Adam all die, so in Christ shall all His people be made alive. To hold fast the historical Adam is to hold fast salvation by imputed righteousness.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The doctrine is rooted in the creation and fall of Genesis and in the apostolic parallel of the two Adams.

expand to see more

Adam was formed of the dust and made a living soul (Gen 2:7).

He was placed under the covenant of works in Eden (Gen 2:16-17).

His transgression brought sin and death upon all his posterity (Rom 5:12).

His guilt and corruption are imputed and conveyed to the race as original sin.

Christ the last Adam answers the first as the head of a redeemed humanity (1 Cor 15:45).

Usage

""In Adam" names the whole race under condemnation by his fall."

""The last Adam" is a title of Christ as the new covenant head."

"The two Adams frame the Reformed doctrine of imputation and federal headship."
